item.title: Science Trivia (Jul 2, 2026)
item.description: What’s cooler than absolute zero? The answer is Science Trivia night at NCMNS! Questions feature a mix of science facts, current news, pop culture and scientific discoveries. Held in the Daily Planet Cafe the first Thursday of each month, this is a great opportunity to mingle with friends, compete for prizes and bragging rights, and perhaps even learn something cool. The Museum closes at 5 PM; the Daily Planet Cafe will remain open. Please copy the URL below to share this page!

item.title: Science Café: Rhinos, Red Pandas, and Hell Pigs, Oh My! (Feb 19, 2026)
item.description: Museum paleontologist Sean Moran holds the cast of a single hell pig molar. Join us in person or watch the livestream on YouTube. Much of North Carolina’s fossil record over the last 100 million years is derived from marine environments, often excluding fossils from terrestrial ecosystems. This talk will explore new fossils collected from Jones County and deposited in the early Miocene, about 20 million years ago, that are beginning to shed light on an unusual land mammal fauna from our state. item.description: Curious about what data science and AI bring to your life everyday? item.title: Teen Science Café: How does Robotic Surgery Work? (Mar 6, 2026)
item.description: Intuitive Surgical revolutionized Minimally Invasive Surgery over 25 years ago with their daVinci robot. 4 Generations of robots later, thousands of daVinci systems have been used to perform over 10 million surgeries worldwide. The daVinci system is one of the best-known examples of a tele-surgery system, where doctors operate by using the surgeon controls at a console in order to move the surgical instruments which are attached to a robot. Join us to hear about the advantages of using robotics ...

item.title: Teen Science Café (Apr 10, 2026)
item.description: Teen Science Cafés bring teens together in an informal setting to learn about science and technology. Cafés happen from 6pm to 7pm the first Friday of each month during the school year. Each café will include a scientist presentation, an interactive activity relating to the discussion, a Q&A session, and time to socialize with other teens who enjoy science. This program is recommended for participants ages 11–17. Cafés will be held in person at the Daily Planet Cafe AND streamed live on YouTube....
